newsitem.title: USA: Aide says Dole not receiving security briefings.
newsitem.headline: Aide says Dole not receiving security briefings.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole has not received any national security briefings from the Clinton administration because so far there has been no need for them, his spokesman said on Wednesday.
Dole campaign spokesman Nelson Warfield said the Central Intelligence Agency contacted the Dole campaign about such briefings Aug. 26, but he suggested there was no immediate need for them.

"Since campaign commentary about the Clinton administration's foreign policy is generally based on past performance, not current operations, to date there has been no need for Senator Dole to receive security briefings," Warfield said.

"As the need develops, Senator Dole will decide how best to use any access to national security briefings," he added. "The administration has made an initial contact with the campaign on this and we expect to discuss it in due course."

It is a tradition in U.S. politics for the president to arrange for his opponent to be briefed on national security to prevent a candidate from making blunders that might jeopardise foreign policy and to present a bipartisan face to the world.
The issue of such briefings came up following President Bill Clinton's decision to attack Iraq with cruise missiles.
On Monday, before the attack, Dole criticised Clinton for "weak leadership."
On Tuesday, after U.S. air and naval forces had fired missiles at Iraq, Dole reversed tack, saying he supported the U.S. servicemen involved and issued no criticism of Clinton.
